item.text:
1. Created alignment **OAK-CT**, beginning at **[3000, 2000]** (E, N), station **10+00**, running north 400 ft to **[3000, 2400]** (station **14+00**). Drew its centerline on **align_MAIN**. On **rd_EP**, drew a radius-45-ft circle centered at [3000, 2400] and two pavement edges from [2986, 2000] and [3014, 2000], trimmed to meet the circle.

2. Tool calls, in order:
   - `get_document_state` — checked document contents and layers.
   - `create_alignment` — `{name:"OAK-CT", start:[3000,2000], legs:[{bearing:"N 0 E", distance:400}], begin_station:"10+00"}`
   - `draw_alignment` — `{alignment:"OAK-CT", layer:"align_MAIN"}`
   - `draw_circle` — `{space:"model", center:[3000,2400], radius:45, layer:"rd_EP"}`
   - `draw_traverse` twice — vertical 450-ft lines starting at `[2986,2000]` and `[3014,2000]`, on `rd_EP`.
   - `trim` — `{boundaries:["CI-001"], targets:[{id:"LN-002",at:[2986,2448]},{id:"LN-003",at:[3014,2448]}]}`

3. One failed attempt: `create_alignment` with bearing `"N"` returned **“cannot read bearing 'N'”**; I retried with `"N 0 E"`. An attempt to draw station-offset edges beyond the alignment also failed: **“station 14+50.00 does not exist on this alignment (10+00.00 to 14+00.00)”**. I worked around that by drawing the edges as lines and trimming them to the circle. The 14-ft offsets give eastings 3000 ± 14; the trimmed intersection is at northing 2400 + √(45² − 14²) ≈ **2442.77**.
